info.long_description: Each is queried on its own WONDER variable, national + state only (no county); a row's `category` is a level of exactly this one dimension, never crossed with another. birth_weight = "Infant Birth Weight 12" (500g bands; finer 14-group and 100g-increment versions exist on the source form but are not pulled). gestational_age = "OE Gestational Age Recode 10", the Obstetric Estimate method NCHS has preferred since ~2014, not the older LMP-based method (a separate, unpulled variable). delivery_method = the plain 3-level "Delivery Method" variable (Vaginal/Cesarean/Unknown; finer "Final Route"/"Delivery Method Expanded" variables exist but aren't pulled) -- cross-checked against the national 2023 rate, 32.3% cesarean, matching published NCHS figures. plurality = single/twin/triplet-or-higher, an exhaustive breakdown (its three categories sum to the geography/year's total births exactly). prenatal_care_trimester = "Trimester Prenatal Care Began"; "No prenatal care" is a real, substantive category here, not collapsed into "Unknown" like WONDER's other non-informative labels. tobacco_use = a simple yes/no/unknown variable (WONDER's separate cigarette-count-by-trimester variables aren't pulled). mothers_education = "Mother's Education"; its raw "Excluded" category (a state's birth-certificate revision not collecting the item at all, a jurisdiction-level gap rather than one record's missingness) is collapsed into "Unknown" here like every other placeholder. marital_status = married/unmarried/unknown.

cdc_wonder_natality.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, National Center for Health Statistics
cdc_wonder_natality.description: Counts of live births from the National Vital Statistics System birth certificate file, as compiled from data provided by the 57 vital statistics jurisdictions through the Vital Statistics Cooperative Program and published through CDC WONDER. Coverage is national, state and county level. County data is published by CDC only for counties of 100,000 or more people; within each state every smaller county is pooled into a single "Unidentified Counties" row under the pseudo-FIPS code SS999, which is retained in the county file but is not a joinable FIPS code. CDC WONDER provides no API for sub-national data (its official API is national-only by policy) so these files are produced by driving the live query form with the Selenium scraper in PopHIVE/wonder-scraper-drowning (scraper/natality_scraper.py), one query per year x geography level x demographic breakdown. Every download is validated against the 'Query Parameters:' footer of the export before it is kept. WONDER's non-informative category rows ("Unknown or Not Stated", "Not Available", "Not Reported", "Not Stated") are collapsed into a single "Unknown" level rather than dropped. Limitations: cells representing 1-9 births are suppressed for confidentiality; breakdowns are single-dimension, not cross-tabulated; and the pull requests counts only, so no birth or fertility rate is included.
cdc_wonder_natality.restrictions: Data Use Restrictions: The Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 242m(d)) provides that the data collected by the National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS) may be used only for the purpose for which they were obtained; any effort to determine the identity of any reported cases, or to use the information for any purpose other than for health statistical reporting and analysis, is against the law. Therefore users will: (1) Use these data for health statistical reporting and analysis only. (2) Do not present or publish birth counts of 9 or fewer or birth rates based on counts of nine or fewer (in figures, graphs, maps, tables, etc.). (3) Make no attempt to learn the identity of any person or establishment included in these data. (4) Make no disclosure or other use of the identity of any person or establishment discovered inadvertently and advise the NCHS Confidentiality Officer of any such discovery: Confidentiality Officer, National Center for Health Statistics, 3311 Toledo Road, Hyattsville, MD 20782. Telephone 888-642-4159. Email: nchsconfidentiality@cdc.gov. Sanctions for Violating Rules: Researchers who violate the terms of the data use restrictions will lose access to WONDER and their sponsors and institutions will be notified. Researchers who are suspected of violating the rules may be prevented from using WONDER until an investigation can be completed. Deliberately making a false statement in any matter within the jurisdiction of any department or agency of the Federal government violates 18 USC 1001 and is punishable by a fine of up to $10,000 or up to 5 years in prison, or both.
